text:
sara: Heads-up: ACME reported 3x p99 for /v1/generate between 2026-03-17 10:03-10:07 UTC. Trace shows sudden hop to ap-south-1. Request IDs: r-9a3c, r-9a3d.

alex: Looking now. Do we have EU edge capacity spike or peering flap? Can you paste the full trace?

sara: Full trace for r-9a3c:
```
eu-west-edge -> internal-proxy-eu (10.12.5.3)
internal-proxy-eu -> global-egress-apac (172.31.4.22)
global-egress-apac -> ap-south-nginx -> dedicated-gpu-ap-south
latencies: 25ms -> 600ms -> 40ms
``` 

priya: That path (global-egress-apac) shouldn't be chosen unless eu peering is down. Do we have any 'X-Region' or customer affinity header on those requests?

sara: Headers from r-9a3c (redacted):
```
:method: POST
:path: /v1/generate
authorization: REDACTED
x-customer-affinity: tenant-acme
x-region: 
x-forwarded-for: 198.51.100.34
```
No x-region present.

michael: We had scheduled peering maintenance with partner-net in eu-west at 10:00 UTC (config change id cfg-2026-0317-01). Some BGP prep was applied then rolled at 10:11 due to noise. That would cause a temporary route withdrawal -> fallback. I'm checking the peering logs.

deploy-bot: rollback completed: cfg-2026-0317-01 -> reverted at 2026-03-17T10:12:04Z :white_check_mark:

sara: After the rollback ACME confirmed p99 dropped back to baseline. Still odd that ap-south was selected instead of us-west as the fallback. Attached routing snapshot (relevant lines):
```
route-policy: prefer-region
  match: customer_affinity
  fallback-order: [regional-egress, global-egress-us, global-egress-apac]
current-active-egress: global-egress-apac (via partner-net)
```

alex: Hypothesis: during the maintenance there was a transient route leak that made ap-south path more 'preferred' from BGP metrics. Need BGP dumps for 10:00-10:12 and peering metrics (AS path length, MED). Can networking team post dumps here?

priya: I'll open a short-term mitigation: prefer regional egress if x-region missing for tenants with sticky affinity. Raising PR now and will also add a runtime alert if global-egress-apac becomes selected for eu tenants.

sara: Thanks — I'll reply to ACME with repro steps: 1) set x-region: eu-west-1 to force; 2) we escalated to networking; 3) full postmortem once BGP dumps are in. I'll DM you logs.

michael: posting peering dump: `bgpdump cfg-2026-0317-01 --since 2026-03-17T09:50Z --until 2026-03-17T10:20Z` output attached to ticket NET-3421.

alex: Strong +1 to the PR. Also let's add a short-lived routing test that simulates a peering withdrawal and confirms fallback order is correct.

sara: Ok. Closing the immediate support escalation. Follow-ups: NET-3421 (BGP dump), RUN-1882 (routing test), PR#4123 (prefer-regional-egress).
